attributes.probed_form: PROBE A (discarded): `case E_DRAGON: CritterLoadFile(lbl_80346C04, "dragon.wad"); break; case E_CHIMERA: CritterLoadFile(lbl_80346C04, "chimera.wad"); break;` with configure.py untouched. Result, `fnasm.py game/game/gamemain init_next_level_8005638C --ours`: `154: addi r4,r30,0` / `164: addi r4,r31,0` / `174: addi r4,r27,40` -- MWCC gave each literal its own base register at offset 0 and pushed the surviving blob base from r30 to r27; the whole call-site block shifted 0x10. Two separate .rodata objects, not a pool. PROBE B (discarded): probe A's source plus configure.py `Object(NonMatching, "game/game/gamemain.c", cflags=[*cflags_demo, "-str reuse,pool,readonly"])` + `python configure.py` + ninja. Result: `14c: addi r4,r31,0` / `15c: addi r4,r31,11` -- ONE base register with compile-time offsets, i.e. the target's addressing shape reproduced, but the pool packs entries TIGHT (11 = len("dragon.wad")+1) where retail 4-aligns them (16 -> 28 = 12). PROBE C (discarded): probe B plus `mw_version="GC/1.2.5"`. Result identical to B -- `14c: addi r4,r31,0` / `15c: addi r4,r31,11`. Both proven compilers pack pooled strings tight. All three reverted with `git checkout -- configure.py src/game/game/gamemain.c`; configure.py + ninja re-run afterwards, `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Rebuild gamemain.c with `-str reuse,pool,readonly` plus the alignment axis and read `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/gamemain init_next_level_8005638C --ours`: if the two literal sites still read `addi r4,rB,0` / `addi r4,rB,11` instead of a 12-byte spacing, the alignment axis is dead and the retail pool layout is unreachable in this archive.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Count-asymmetric against the current source in the measured form: with literals and no pool flag the function GREW and consumed two extra callee-saved base registers (r30 and r31 each held one literal's address at offset 0, the pool base moved to r27, and every call site shifted by 0x10). With the pool flag the count came back to shape but the offsets were wrong (11 vs 12), so the residual is DATA layout, not instruction count.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- the target side is fully decoded: lbl_80112788 is 0x24C of 4-byte-aligned NUL-terminated literals dumped from orig/GUNE5D/sys/main.dol, and the target codegen (one lis/addi materialising r30, then `addi r4,r30,N` per site) was read from fnasm.py. What is NOT screened is whether any point in the mwcc option space 4-aligns pooled entries.
hypothesis.statement: gamemain.c's string-blob externs (lbl_80112788, lbl_80112370) can be replaced by REAL STRING LITERALS -- the true Midway source -- if the pooled object our compiler emits can be made to 4-byte-align its entries. Our archive pools (one base register, compile-time offsets: the right SHAPE) but packs entries tight: measured 'dragon.wad' at +0 and 'chimera.wad' at +11 where retail has +16 and +28. The untried axis is the pool-entry ALIGNMENT, not the pooling: try `-align` variants, and try the pool flag on a TU whose blob is already fully decoded so the expected layout is known before the build.
